messages:
liz_research: heads-up — bringing up Cascade-7B in our eval cluster. License shows as 'NC-ATTRIB-1.0' (link below). Quick legal question: can we 4-bit quantize and host on Dedicated, or ship quantized weights to enterprise customers?

sam_legal: short answer: NC = non-commercial, so shipping to paying customers is likely disallowed. Need to check whether 'hosting as a service' counts as distribution under this specific license. Please paste the license text or link.

anna_ml: fwiw the plan is just a deterministic quant transform (bitsandbytes style), no fine-tuning. Does that count as a derivative?

sam_legal: transforms that create new weight files are typically treated as derivatives. The license language matters but "no commercial use" usually prohibits making those transformed weights available to paying customers or including them in paid products.

mike_infra: to add practical context: Dedicated customers get artifacts copied into their VPC/instances. That would be us transferring a tarball to a customer environment.

liz_research: ok so I see three paths: 1) ask upstream for a commercial/enterprise license; 2) keep model behind Redwood-hosted API but restrict to internal/research use only; 3) avoid distributing the weight files at all and only ship inferences from a sealed environment.

sam_legal: correct. Also note attribution clause — if we do anything public (docs, model card, or redistributed weights) we must retain the original attribution and include the license text and model provenance (SHA sums, upstream repo link).

anna_ml: question: what about serving embeddings to customers? Are embeddings derivative outputs or allowed under NC?

sam_legal: embeddings are a gray area. Some licenses explicitly carve out model outputs; others don't. For NC licenses I'm cautious: embedding vectors derived from the model are usually considered outputs, but some licensors claim rights over outputs. Don't expose embeddings externally without written permission.

deploy-bot: model card + license: https://models.example/cascade-7b/model-card.md 
license: https://models.example/cascade-7b/LICENSE.txt

liz_research: action items: @sam_legal to draft a short upstream contact explaining intended commercial uses and request a commercial license or exception; @anna_ml run the quant smoke test but only in the research-only cluster (no exporting artifact tarballs); @mike_infra hold off on provisioning Dedicated artifact transfer.

sam_legal: will draft the note today and cc @liz_research. If upstream refuses, recommend we either (a) replace with a permissively licensed model or (b) provide inference-only via Redwood-hosted research enclave and log all access.

anna_ml: noted — I'll record the exact quantization steps and hashes in the internal eval doc so legal can reference the transform.

mike_infra: blocking Dedicated move until we have a legal greenlight.

liz_research: perfect. thanks all. :thumbsup:
